scenario.note: The output for year 4 is limited to 80% of the output for year 3.
Limits the capacity built in year 5 to 10% of the total capacity built in years 1-4.
The output for year 2 is constrained to be at most 25% of the output for year 5.
Capacity built in year 5 cannot exceed 20% of the total capacity built in years 1-4.
Two relative limits: stock is at most 75% of total capacity built; year 3 capacity built is at least 60% of year 5 capacity built.
Year 2 output is limited to 5% of the total output from years 1, 3, 4, and 5.
The total output produced across all industries and years is bounded by 90% of the total stock held across the same periods.
The first rule limits year 5 output to 25% of year 3 output. The second rule requires total capacity built to be at least 50% of total output produced.
Year 6 output must be at least 10% of the total output from years 1 to 5.
A relative rule comparing the capacity built in year 3 to that in year 5.
Limits the total production in year 4 to 50% of the total production in year 3.
The stock in year 2 must be at least twice the stock in year 1.
Steel production must be at least 1.25 times transport production.
Capacity built in year 3 cannot exceed 5% of the total capacity built in other years.
The stock in year 5 is limited to 60% of the stock in year 2.
A relative rule comparing the sum of production for transport to twice the sum for steel.
The total capacity built over years 1–5 must be at least 1.5 times the total stock held over the same period.
